Balanced variation and abundance gradients of abundance dissimilarity

Source: R/beta_partition.r
bray_balanced.Rd

Baselga's partition of the Bray-Curtis and Ruzicka (Soergel) dissimilarities between two samples into balanced variation in abundance (some features gain what others lose) and abundance gradients (every feature is less abundant in one sample).

Usage

bray_balanced(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  norm = "none",
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

bray_gradient(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  norm = "none",
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

soergel_balanced(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  norm = "none",
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

soergel_gradient(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  norm = "none",
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of count data (samples \(\times\) features). Values must not be negative.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

norm

Normalize the incoming counts first: 'none' (the default, as betapart and abdiv), 'percent' (relative abundances), 'chord', 'hellinger' or 'binary'. 'clr', 'rclr' and 'log' give negative values and are refused.

pairs

Which combinations of samples should distances be calculated for? The default value (NULL) calculates all-vs-all. Provide a numeric or logical vector specifying positions in the distance matrix to calculate. See examples.

clust

Whether and how to cluster the samples (rows and columns) before returning the distance matrix: NULL (the default) or FALSE to keep them in their input order, or one of stats::hclust()'s linkage methods, "average" (UPGMA), "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty" (WPGMA), "median" or "centroid", or "pcoa" to order them along the first axis of pcoa(). Clustering reorders the samples of the result, with their labels (samples without names are labelled with their positions in the input): its order attribute gives each one's position in the input, so that meta[attr(d, "order"), ] lines metadata up with them. ecodive's ordinations and tests put the samples back in their input order before analysing them, so give them metadata in its usual order. Other packages see the reordered matrix: give them metadata reordered by order, or matched by name. The matrix's display list keeps clust (FALSE as "none"; see ecodive_display), which plot.ecodive_dist() follows: with NULL it clusters the samples for the heatmap ("average"), and with "none" it keeps their order. clust needs every distance, so it cannot be used with pairs. rho_p()'s similarities are clustered as \(1 - \rho_p\).

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

Value

A distance matrix: a dist object of class c("ecodive_dist", "dist"), as beta_div() returns.

Details

With abundances \(x_k\) and \(y_k\) of each feature in the two samples, \(A = \sum_k \min(x_k, y_k)\) (the abundance they share), \(B = \sum_k \max(x_k - y_k, 0)\) and \(C = \sum_k \max(y_k - x_k, 0)\) (what only the first and only the second has); Baselga (2013, 2017):

FunctionComponentFormula
bray()Bray-Curtis dissimilarity (total)\(\frac{B + C}{2A + B + C}\)
bray_balanced()balanced variation, \(d_{BC-bal}\)\(\frac{\min(B, C)}{A + \min(B, C)}\)
bray_gradient()abundance gradient, \(d_{BC-gra}\)\(d_{BC} - d_{BC-bal}\)
soergel()Ruzicka dissimilarity (total)\(\frac{B + C}{A + B + C}\)
soergel_balanced()balanced variation, \(d_{RUZ-bal}\)\(\frac{2\min(B, C)}{A + 2\min(B, C)}\)
soergel_gradient()abundance gradient, \(d_{RUZ-gra}\)\(d_{RUZ} - d_{RUZ-bal}\)

soergel() is the Ruzicka dissimilarity (vegan's quantitative Jaccard), so its components are named after it; "ruzicka_balanced" and "ruzicka_gradient" select them in beta_div(). The two components add up to the total, bray() or soergel(). On presence/absence data (norm = 'binary') they are the turnover and nestedness of sorensen_turnover().

When a sample is empty (all zeros), both components are undefined (NaN), as in abdiv and betapart. Neither is a metric.

Same names in other packages: abdiv's functions are named bray_curtis_balanced(), bray_curtis_gradient(), ruzicka_balanced() and ruzicka_gradient(), taking two vectors; they give the same values. betapart's beta.pair.abund() returns all three matrices of a family, as beta_partition() does.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Baselga, A. (2013). Separating the two components of abundance-based dissimilarity: balanced changes in abundance vs. abundance gradients. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4, 552-557. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12029

Baselga, A. (2017). Partitioning abundance-based multiple-site dissimilarity into components: balanced variation in abundance and abundance gradients. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 8, 799-808. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12693

See also

beta_partition() for the three matrices of a family at once, beta_partition_multi() for whole sets of samples, beta_div().

Other Partitioned metrics: beta_partition(), beta_partition_multi(), sorensen_turnover()

Examples

    bray_balanced(ex_counts)
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Bray-Curtis Balanced Variation
#>       Saliva  Gums Nose
#> Gums   0.27
#> Nose   0.922 0.968
#> Stool  0.988 0.989 0.99
#> # Attributes: method
    bray_gradient(ex_counts)
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Bray-Curtis Abundance Gradient
#>        Saliva    Gums    Nose
#> Gums  0.321
#> Nose  0.0384  0.00208
#> Stool 0.00326 0.00205 0.00238
#> # Attributes: method

    # Of relative abundances.
    soergel_balanced(ex_counts, norm = 'percent')
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Ruzicka Balanced Variation
#>       Saliva  Gums  Nose
#> Gums   0.598
#> Nose   0.985 0.986
#> Stool  0.995 0.996 0.996
#> # Attributes: method
